cards.explanation: The answer is Herod. Manaen had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch (Acts 13:1). He's listed right there with the prophets and teachers at Antioch. Friends, I think that's quite a background for one teacher.

The answer is Barnabas and Saul. The Holy Spirit says, “Set apart for Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.” (Acts 13:2) Barnabas is the first name in the list and Saul is the last. The Spirit picked the two on the ends, and the three in the middle are still part of the team.

The answer is that hands are laid on them. After they had fasted and prayed, they laid their hands on them and sent them off (Acts 13:3). Hands on Barnabas and Saul, and then off they went. Friends, I know a little about hands changing your day, because Mother Miller's hands once pulled me out of a 25-cent bin. Mine came with flour and a price sticker, though.

The answer is Cyprus. Barnabas and Saul went down to Seleucia and sailed from there to Cyprus (Acts 13:4). That's an island, so there was no walking this one off. They went by boat, and the Holy Spirit sent them.

The answer is synagogues. When they arrived at Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the Jewish synagogues (Acts 13:5). Friends, a synagogue is a Jewish meeting place. That's where they started telling people God's word.

The answer is that he wants to hear the word of God. The proconsul, a man of intelligence, summoned Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear the word of God (Acts 13:7). Sergius Paulus is the proconsul, a Roman governor of the island. He sent for them because he wanted to listen.

The answer is that he tries to turn the proconsul from the faith. Elymas the sorcerer opposed them and tried to turn the proconsul from the faith (Acts 13:8). Friends, the proconsul, Sergius Paulus, is the one who summoned Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear the word of God (Acts 13:7). Elymas is the one who opposed them.

The answer is False. Paul says, “…for a time you will be blind and unable to see the light of the sun.” (Acts 13:11) He says for a time, friends, and not one word about forever. I think that matters, because a time is something that ends.

The answer is that he gropes around for someone to lead him. Immediately mist and darkness came over him, and he groped about, seeking someone to lead him by the hand (Acts 13:11). Friends, a man who just opposed them is now reaching around for a hand to hold. I think that's a hard moment to see.

The answer is True. When the proconsul saw what had happened, he believed, for he was astonished at the teaching about the Lord (Acts 13:12). He's the one who asked to hear God's word, friends. In the end he believed.
